text.VERDICT: Nothing visible lost: yes. Every one of the 218 re-encoded pictures scores at least as well as the q82 pictures you already looked at and passed (the gear icon, Pokey's story picture, the World 2 backdrop), on every score. Anything that scored worse, and every dark picture, stays exactly as shipped.
text.BLACK: It is World 10's far storm sky (backdrops/w10-far.webp): 72% of it is near black, and 58% is smooth dark sky with no texture. At q82 and q75 the smooth dark gradient breaks into soft 16 px blocks and blotches (WebP's macroblocks), most visible right under the lightning. Its scores at q82 look fine on paper (SSIM 0.992, PSNR 45 dB), because those scores forgive errors in flat dark areas, so I did not trust them alone: the dark rule and SSIMULACRA2 (75.2, the only score that marks it worse than the pictures you passed) catch it.
text.HOW: Each q82 picture was decoded and compared with its original on the parts you can see (alpha above zero; transparency is copied losslessly and checked identical). Four scores: SSIM (1.0 = identical), PSNR, the worst 32 px tile's SSIM, the worst dark tile's error, and SSIMULACRA2 (a perceptual score, 90 = indistinguishable, 80 = not noticeable at normal distance). The pass marks are set by your own eye: a picture is flagged and kept as shipped if any score is worse than the worst q82 picture you passed on the AS-1 page (SSIM 0.98, worst tile 0.90, PSNR 35 dB, dark tile 36.5 dB, SSIMULACRA2 78.5), or if it has smooth dark areas as damaged as the black picture's. Sizes are in the same MB as the AS-1 page.
